statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an additive category.
Let $f, g : B_\bullet \to C_\bullet$ be morphisms
of chain complexes. Suppose given morphisms of chain
complexes $a : A_\bullet \to B_\bullet$, and
$c : C_\bullet \to D_\bullet$.
If $\{h_i : B_i \to C_{i + 1}\}$ defines a homotopy
between $f$ and $g$, then $\{c_{i + 1} \circ h_i \circ a_i\}$
defines a homotopy between $c \circ f \circ a$ and
$c \circ g \circ a$.
hypotheses: $a:A_\bullet\to B_\bullet$, $f,g:B_\bullet\to C_\bullet$, $c:C_\bullet\to D_\bullet$ chain maps; $h_i:B_i\to C_{i+1}$ a homotopy between $f,g$.

review_note: Category of chain complexes in an abelian category is abelian and its mono/epi/exactness tests occur degreewise. This review compared the independently parsed Stage A statement against its pinned original theorem excerpt; no proofs or remarks accessed. Preliminary, not authoritative.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The category of chain complexes in $\mathcal{A}$ is
abelian.
\item A morphism of complexes
$f : A_\bullet \to B_\bullet$ is injective
if and only if each $f_n : A_n \to B_n$ is injective.
\item A morphism of complexes
$f : A_\bullet \to B_\bullet$ is surjective
if and only if each $f_n : A_n \to B_n$ is surjective.
\item A sequence of chain complexes
$$
A_\bullet \xrightarrow{f} B_\bullet \xrightarrow{g} C_\bullet
$$
is exact at $B_\bullet$ if and only if each sequence
$$
A_i \xrightarrow{f_i} B_i \xrightarrow{g_i} C_i
$$
is exact at $B_i$.
\end{enumerate}
conclusions: The category of chain complexes is abelian; its monics, epics and exactness are characterized degreewise.

Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The category of chain complexes in $\mathcal{A}$ is
abelian.
\item A morphism of complexes
$f : A_\bullet \to B_\bullet$ is injective
if and only if each $f_n : A_n \to B_n$ is injective.
\item A morphism of complexes
$f : A_\bullet \to B_\bullet$ is surjective
if and only if each $f_n : A_n \to B_n$ is surjective.
\item A sequence of chain complexes
$$
A_\bullet \xrightarrow{f} B_\bullet \xrightarrow{g} C_\bullet
$$
is exact at $B_\bullet$ if and only if each sequence
$$
A_i \xrightarrow{f_i} B_i \xrightarrow{g_i} C_i
$$
is exact at $B_i$.
\end{enumerate}

review_note: Chain-homotopic maps induce equal homology maps, hence a chain homotopy equivalence is a quasi-isomorphism. This review compared the independently parsed Stage A statement against its pinned original theorem excerpt; no proofs or remarks accessed. Preliminary, not authoritative.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If the maps $f, g : A_\bullet \to B_\bullet$ are
homotopic, then the induced maps $H_i(f)$ and $H_i(g)$
are equal.
\item If the map $f : A_\bullet \to B_\bullet$ is a homotopy
equivalence, then $f$ is a quasi-isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}
conclusions: Homotopic chain maps induce equal homology maps; a homotopy equivalence is a quasi-isomorphism.

statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Suppose that
$$
0 \to
A_\bullet \to
B_\bullet \to
C_\bullet \to
0
$$
is a short exact sequence of chain complexes of $\mathcal{A}$.
Then there is a canonical long exact homology sequence
$$
\xymatrix{
\ldots & \ldots & \ldots \ar[lld] \\
H_i(A_\bullet) \ar[r] & H_i(B_\bullet) \ar[r] & H_i(C_\bullet) \ar[lld] \\
H_{i - 1}(A_\bullet) \ar[r] &
H_{i - 1}(B_\bullet) \ar[r] &
H_{i - 1}(C_\bullet) \ar[lld] \\
\ldots & \ldots & \ldots \\
}
$$
hypotheses: $0\to A_\bullet\to B_\bullet\to C_\bullet\to0$ is short exact in chain complexes of an abelian category.
conclusions: A canonical long exact homology sequence exists with the source's $H_i(C)\to H_{i-1}(A)$ indexing.

statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Suppose that
$$
0 \to
A^\bullet \to
B^\bullet \to
C^\bullet \to
0
$$
is a short exact sequence of cochain complexes of $\mathcal{A}$.
Then there is a long exact cohomology sequence
$$
\xymatrix{
\ldots & \ldots & \ldots \ar[lld] \\
H^i(A^\bullet) \ar[r] &
H^i(B^\bullet) \ar[r] &
H^i(C^\bullet) \ar[lld] \\
H^{i + 1}(A^\bullet) \ar[r] &
H^{i + 1}(B^\bullet) \ar[r] &
H^{i + 1}(C^\bullet) \ar[lld] \\
\ldots & \ldots & \ldots \\
}
$$
The construction produces long exact cohomology sequences
which are functorial in the short exact
sequence and compatible with shifts as in
the cochain-shift identification $H^j(K[k])\cong H^{j+k}(K)$ using the signed shift differential.
hypotheses: $0\to A^\bullet\to B^\bullet\to C^\bullet\to0$ is short exact in cochain complexes of an abelian category.
conclusions: There is a functorial long exact cohomology sequence with degree-raising connecting maps, compatible with shifted cohomology $H^j(K[k])\cong H^{j+k}(K)$.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain}
\begin{slogan}
Short exact sequences of complexes give rise to long exact sequences
of (co)homology.
\end{slogan}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Suppose that
$$
0 \to
A^\bullet \to
B^\bullet \to
C^\bullet \to
0
$$
is a short exact sequence of cochain complexes of $\mathcal{A}$.
Then there is a long exact cohomology sequence
$$
\xymatrix{
\ldots & \ldots & \ldots \ar[lld] \\
H^i(A^\bullet) \ar[r] &
H^i(B^\bullet) \ar[r] &
H^i(C^\bullet) \ar[lld] \\
H^{i + 1}(A^\bullet) \ar[r] &
H^{i + 1}(B^\bullet) \ar[r] &
H^{i + 1}(C^\bullet) \ar[lld] \\
\ldots & \ldots & \ldots \\
}
$$
The construction produces long exact cohomology sequences
which are functorial in the short exact
sequence and compatible with shifts as in
Definition \ref{definition-cohomology-shift}.
